title: Quentin and the Lantern
premise: In the autumn of 1918, Elodie Okafor, an apprentice clockmaker in a small French-adjacent border town, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock, only to discover her late master's hidden ledger — a record of names, debts, and quiet rescues that made him the town's unofficial conscience. When the army requisitions the town for its final offensive, a deserter named Quentin arrives seeking the ledger, believing it holds proof that can save a condemned comrade. As shells fall closer and the armistice negotiations stall, Elodie, Quentin, and the workshop's ragtag found family must finish repairing both the clock and the ledger's unfinished business before the fighting ends and the truth is buried forever. The book ends at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day: the clock strikes, the ledger is read aloud in the ruined square, and Elodie inherits not just the workshop but the duty it represents.
about_author: Ivo Sterling is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring mechanical clocks in provincial European collections. Their fiction explores how ordinary objects outlast the people who trusted them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Elodie Okafor, POV. Summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, she finds the workshop of her late master Augustin untouched since his death, his tools still warm with habit. She believes history happens elsewhere, to other people. Emotional beat: grief disguised as professional pride.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Behind the clock's faceplate she discovers Augustin's secret ledger: decades of names — debtors forgiven, deserters sheltered, letters smuggled. She realizes the town's kindness had an architect. Emotional beat: awe curdling into doubt about the man she revered.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell Through the Door
chapters.summary: Quentin, POV. A wounded deserter from the requisitioned garrison stumbles into the workshop seeking 'the lantern keeper.' He carries half a page torn from a ledger naming a condemned comrade. Emotional beat: desperation meeting unexpected shelter.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Army officers seize the town; the observatory becomes a signal post and the workshop is slated for confiscation. Captain Vasseur demands all records, ledgers included. Emotional beat: the intrusion of history into the domestic, exactly what Elodie feared.

chapters.title: What Quentin Knew
chapters.summary: Quentin, POV. He confesses he deserted to find proof his friend Luc was scapegoated for a stolen supply convoy; the ledger holds the real thief's name. Elodie hides the book inside the clock's case. Emotional beat: two strangers choosing trust over safety.

chapters.title: The Found Family Assembles
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Marguerite the baker, old Tomas the bell-ringer, and boy-soldier Petit gather in the workshop as the town empties. Each owes their name a place in Augustin's ledger. Emotional beat: warmth kindling inside siege walls.

chapters.title: Gears Against Deadlines
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Repairing the master clock becomes cover work; by day she serves the army, by night she hunts the ledger for Luc's exculpating entry. Emotional beat: purpose replacing passivity.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Suspicion
chapters.summary: Captain Vasseur, POV. The captain notices missing pages and begins watching Elodie, himself haunted by orders he cannot refuse. Emotional beat: antagonist rendered human, threat sharpening.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Quentin, POV. The entry naming the true thief — a supply officer now on Vasseur's own staff — is among pages torn out long ago. They realize Augustin was silenced, perhaps murdered. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as danger.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Debt
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. She reveals Augustin once hid her husband from a firing squad; she has kept his duplicate key and knows where he hid sensitive papers: inside the observatory's lantern room. Emotional beat: gratitude transformed into courage.

chapters.title: Climbing the Dark
chapters.summary: Quentin and Elodie, alternating. Under blackout they climb to the lantern room and find Augustin's cache — including correspondence proving the officer's theft. Shells fall nearer; the clock above them ticks toward ruin. Emotional beat: terror braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Petit's War
chapters.summary: Petit, POV. The sixteen-year-old messenger is ordered to report 'strangers' in the workshop. He lies for the first time. Emotional beat: innocence spending itself to protect a family it chose.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Vasseur confronts her with the torn-page evidence; she deflects by offering to restore the master clock as the army's 'symbol of order.' He gives her until the armistice — rumored within days. Emotional beat: bargaining under a blade.

chapters.title: The Officer's Name
chapters.summary: Quentin, POV. The cache identifies Major Renard as the convoy thief. But delivering it means accusing an officer through channels that will bury it. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins to take shape.

chapters.title: Tomas Rings False
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Ordered to ring the armistice bells prematurely as a morale test, he instead uses the bell code to warn the household of a raid. Emotional beat: an old man's quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Soldiers search the workshop; the ledger survives inside the clock's pendulum case, but Quentin is taken. Emotional beat: loss striking the found family's center.

chapters.title: Cell and Clockwork
chapters.summary: Quentin, POV. Imprisoned beside Luc, Quentin learns Vasseur has quietly read the recovered pages and wavers. Elodie negotiates: the full truth for the prisoners' lives. Emotional beat: hope negotiated in whispers.

chapters.title: Renard Strikes
chapters.summary: Vasseur, POV. Major Renard moves to destroy the evidence and the observatory itself, ordering the tower shelled as 'a signal hazard.' Vasseur must choose. Emotional beat: the antagonist's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Hour Approaches
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. With the town under bombardment, she races to finish the clock's escapement so it can strike the armistice hour — the moment the whole town will be listening. Emotional beat: craft as resistance.

chapters.title: Armistice Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vasseur arrests Renard using the ledger's proof, freeing Quentin and Luc; the family repairs the tower by lamplight through the night. Emotional beat: exhausted, trembling readiness.

chapters.title: When the Lantern Burns
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. At eleven o'clock on the eleventh day, the master clock strikes and Elodie reads the ledger aloud in the ruined square — every name, every rescue. The town hears its own hidden history. Emotional beat: catharsis, grief, and vindication.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Elodie, POV. Weeks later, she reopens the workshop, hangs Augustin's lantern in the door, and writes new names in the ledger — beginning with Quentin's. Emotional beat: the past handed forward, a family made official.
